extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, law students, and judges researching patent doctrines
extracted.subtask_description: An indexed list of patent-law case holdings and doctrinal principles summarizing standards for patentability, infringement, remedies, procedure, and related rights drawn from reported cases. Useful as a quick-reference of legal criteria and interpretive rules applied in U.S. patent litigation and prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue of combination-patent to cover elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-issue of combination-patent to cover elements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexed as noted in Machine Co. (1882). Indicates re-issue practice for combination patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of invention or discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessity of invention or discovery
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General principle cited (Omnty of Fond dn Lac (1886)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes in elements of combination
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes in elements of combination
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed under Maynadier v. Tenney (1877) — relevant to identity and infringement of combinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue of generic patent cannot claim different species
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-issue of generic patent cannot claim different species from original
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From McClintock, Ex parte (1880) — limitation on scope of re-issue claims vis-à-vis original disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retrospective acts creating patent privilege
rubrics_metrics.description: Retrospective acts creating patent privilege
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical/principle note (McClurg v. Kingsland (1843)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction to practice necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduction to practice necessary
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears repeatedly (McComb v. Brodie (1872); Morton v. New York Eye Infirmary (1862)); principle for priority and patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle, idea or abstraction not patentable
rubrics_metrics.description: Principle, idea or abstraction not patentable
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited (multiple cases) as a core limit on patentable subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle reduced to practice patentable
rubrics_metrics.description: Principle reduced to practice patentable
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a principle is embodied in a practical application it may be patentable (cited contrasts with abstract principles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Damages measured by loss of plaintiff's sales
rubrics_metrics.description: Damages measured by loss of plaintiff's sales
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure of damages cited (McComb v. Brodie).

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination-patent not infringed by use of part
rubrics_metrics.description: Combination-patent not infringed by use of part
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From McCormick v. Manny (1855) — limits on infringement of combination patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: License fee the measure of damages
rubrics_metrics.description: License fee the measure of damages
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noted (Seymour) — in some cases license fee is used to calculate damages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ascertainment of profits
rubrics_metrics.description: Ascertainment of profite
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referenced as an evidentiary/measuring concept for remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test of design
rubrics_metrics.description: Test of design
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referenced in McCrea v. Holdsworth (1865) — standard for design patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joinder of subprocesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Joinder of subprocesses
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed (McDougall, Ex parte) — relates to claims that combine processes or subprocesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product may be protected though machine-patent expired
rubrics_metrics.description: Product may be protected by its patent though the machine-patent has expired
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noted in McKay v. Dibert — interaction of different patents on product vs. machine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patented article sold by grantee released from monopoly
rubrics_metrics.description: Patented article sold by grantee released from the monopoly
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sale by grantee can exhaust certain rights (Wooster) — exhaustion doctrine precursor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of co-operation of combination elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Duration of the co-operation of combination elements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant to combination claims and their functioning over time (McKesson v. Carnrick).

rubrics_metrics.name: Laches forfeits right to injunction
rubrics_metrics.description: Laches forfeits right to injunction
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equitable doctrine affecting remedies (McLaughlin v. People's R. R.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public use by inventor is an abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Public use by the inventor himself is an abandonment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public use bar to patentability (McMillin v. Barclay).

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel by inaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Estoppel of plaintiff in equity by inaction
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equitable estoppel limits relief when patentee has inacted (McMillin v. Barclay).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim for improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim for improvement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ex parte and other decisions on claiming improvements (McMurray, Ex parte).

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure of reasonable diligence in reducing to practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure of reasonable diligence in reducing to practice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard for priority disputes and interference (McTammany, Jr. v. Needham).

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs taxed for nominal damages verdicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs taxed when verdict gives nominal damages
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Litigation-cost allocation principle (Merchant v. Lewis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of improvement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirement for specification to describe improvements (Merrill v. Yeomans).

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure of profits
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure of profite
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in equitable accounting of defendant's profits.

rubrics_metrics.name: State court jurisdiction despite collateral attack on monopoly
rubrics_metrics.description: State court has jurisdiction though monopoly collaterally attacked
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural jurisdiction note (Merserole v. Union Paper Collar Co.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment and grant distinguished
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignment and grant distinguished
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinction relevant to rights conveyed (Meyer v. Bailey).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of amended patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Scope of amended patent
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits on amendments to patents and their scope (Maxheimer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive act can be instantaneous
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventive act instantaneous
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conception/reduction-to-practice doctrines acknowledging instantaneous inventive acts (Middletown Tool Co. v. Judd).

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue not to enlarge claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-issue not to enlarge claims
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Re-issue limitations (Miller v. Brass Co.; multiple entries on re-issue doctrine).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to re-issue lost by unreasonable delay
rubrics_metrics.description: Right to re-issue lost by unreasonable delay
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delay can bar re-issue remedies (Miller v. Brass Co.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Actual parties in interest control the suit
rubrics_metrics.description: Actual parties in interest control the suit
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Who may prosecute an infringement suit (Liggett & Myers Tobacco Co. v. Smith).

rubrics_metrics.name: Infringement of patent for design
rubrics_metrics.description: Infringement of patent for design
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards differ for design patents (case citations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Process and product separately patentable
rubrics_metrics.description: Process and product separately patentable
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both process and product may be independently patentable (Hilligan & Higgins Glue Co. v. Upton).

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty of manufacture
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty of manufacture
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novelty requirement applied to manufactured items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity between original and re-issue claims shown by comparing them
rubrics_metrics.description: Identity between original and re-issue claims shown by comparing them, excluding parol evidence
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test for identity in re-issue proceedings (Hilligan & Higgins Glue Co. v. Upton).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision of Commissioner on re-issue how far conclusive
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision of Commissioner on re-issue how far conclusive
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deference and finality of Patent Office decisions regarding re-issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Race of diligence between rival inventors
rubrics_metrics.description: Race of diligence between rival inventors
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority doctrine where rival inventors race to reduction to practice (Millward v. Barnes; Packard v. Sandford).

rubrics_metrics.name: License to use specific machine endures under extension
rubrics_metrics.description: License to use specific machine endures under extension
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effect of term extensions on license rights (Mitchell v. Hawley).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer of exclusive right not a mere license
rubrics_metrics.description: Transfer of exclusive right to make and sell not a mere license
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conveys ownership beyond a license (Mitchell v. Hawley).

rubrics_metrics.name: Vendee's rights to use patented article
rubrics_metrics.description: Vendee of patented article can use it without limit as to time; can repair it; cannot rebuild it
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Buyer-rights/exhaustion and repair vs. reconstruction distinctions (Mitchell v. Hawley; related cases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Monopoly in inventions (historical principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Monopoly in inventions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foundational statement of patent privilege (V. Reynolds (1713) and other early cases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability of an art
rubrics_metrics.description: Patentability of an art
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Art (process) can be patentable subject matter (Tilghman).

rubrics_metrics.name: Very dangerous inventions not useful
rubrics_metrics.description: Very dangerous inventions not useful
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utility requirement may exclude inventions harmful to the public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application to conform to legal requisites
rubrics_metrics.description: Application to conform to legal requisites
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal requirements for patent applications (Moffitt v. Gaar).

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue the basis of subsequent rights and suits
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-issue the basis of all subsequent rights and suits
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Re-issue controls downstream enforcement (Moffitt v. Gaar; Peck v. Collins).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of delay of prior inventor in applying for patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Effect of delay of prior inventor in applying for a patent
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delay may impact priority or estoppel (Monce v. Adams; Rice v. Winchester).

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination-patent infringed by use of elements and subcombinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Combination-patent infringed by use of elements and subcombinations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Infringement can occur by practicing portions that perform the claimed cooperation (Moody v. Fiske).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignees must sue jointly for infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignees must sue jointly for infringement when [conditions specified]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural requirement for assignees (Moore v. Marsh).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature of patent privilege
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature of patent privilege
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent privilege conceptualized in multiple cases (Morgan's patent, In re; Morgan v. Seaward).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure is consideration for monopoly
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure the consideration for the monopoly
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foundational bargain of patent system: disclosure in exchange for exclusion (Morgan v. Seaward).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substance and form in inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Substance and form in inventions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinction when construing patents (Morgan cases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility degree immaterial / Utility necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Utility, degree of, immaterial; utility necessary
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utility requirement — existence of utility matters, not degree (cited multiple times).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sales as a mode of abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Sales as a mode of abandonment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sale or public distribution may trigger abandonment/public-use bar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalents in improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Equivalents in improvements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Doctrine of equivalents applied to improvements (Morley Sewing Mach. Co. v. Lancaster).

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvement patentable
rubrics_metrics.description: Improvement patentable
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patents can cover improvements on earlier inventions (Morris v. Bransom).

rubrics_metrics.name: Injunction issued despite consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Injunction issued whatever its consequences
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equitable relief may issue even if consequences are severe (V. Lowell Mfg. Co.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpatentable discoveries
rubrics_metrics.description: Unpatentable discoveries
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes discoveries (unpatentable) from inventions (Morton v. New York Eye Infirmary).

rubrics_metrics.name: Description addressed to those skilled in the art
rubrics_metrics.description: Description addressed to those skilled in the art; description intelligible to those skilled in the art
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written-description and enablement standards require communication to skilled artisans (Mowry v. Whitney).

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeal of patent in public interest and for fraud
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeal proper when patent obtained by fraud; repeal procured by bill in equity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equitable remedies available to cancel patents obtained by fraud or for public-interest reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use with new object
rubrics_metrics.description: Use with new object
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior use may be excused if used for a new object (Mantz v. Foster et al.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim for one form covers all forms (overbroad claims void)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim for one form of the invention covers all forms (void)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims that attempt to cover all modes of effecting a result may be invalid (O'Reilly v. Morse; other cites).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unreasonable delay in disclaiming / disclaimer pending suit
rubrics_metrics.description: Unreasonable delay in disclaiming; disclaimer pending suit
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness of disclaimers affects validity/enforcement of re-issues and claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity shown on motion for injunction by judgments or acquiescence
rubrics_metrics.description: Validity shown on motion for injunction by judgments or acquiescence; acquiescence as proof of validity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural showing for preliminary relief; acquiescence can be evidence of validity but must be of some duration and assertive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior publication must communicate invention to public
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior publication must communicate the same invention to the public
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior publication is a statutory/publicity bar only when it teaches the invention (Palmer, Ex parte; Plimpton v. Malcolmson).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent for apparatus may cover process also
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent for apparatus may cover process also
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relationship between apparatus and process claims (New Process Fermentation Co. v. Koch).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chemical process patentable (not its result)
rubrics_metrics.description: Chemical process, not its result, patentable
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process that changes chemicals may be patentable irrespective of final result (Maus).

rubrics_metrics.name: New combination of arts patentable
rubrics_metrics.description: New combination of arts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combining distinct arts may produce patentable subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentee bound by the patent as accepted from Patent Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Patentee bound by the patent as he accepts it from the Patent Office
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patentee cannot claim broader rights than the issued patent (New York Belting & Packing Co. v. Sibley).

rubrics_metrics.name: Stam ping in expectation of patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Stamping in expectation of patent
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marked articles and stamping practices discussed as evidentiary of notice (Nichols v. Newell).

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility of result as evidence of novelty and inventive skill
rubrics_metrics.description: Utility of result as evidence of novelty and inventive skill in the means
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Showing a useful result may support novelty and inventiveness in the means used (Pennock, Ex parte).

rubrics_metrics.name: True and first inventor / effect of public use by rival
rubrics_metrics.description: True and first inventor; effect of public use by rival inventor
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority rules and effects of intervening public uses on entitlement (Daye and other authorities).

rubrics_metrics.name: State police power over sale of patented inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Police power of State over sale of patented inventions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may regulate sale/commerce in patented goods under police powers (State cases cited).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior use in public & public use definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior use in public; public use is use in ordinary way without restrictions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public-use bar defined; secret/experimental use treated differently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implied license to vendee from recovery of royalties
rubrics_metrics.description: Implied license to vendee from recovery of royalties against unlawful vendor
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equitable implied-licence doctrines when title/royalties issues arise (Perrigo v. Spaulding; Steam cases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment recording rules (unrecorded assignment valid inter partes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignment unrecorded valid inter partes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recordation affects third-party rights but not inter partes validity (Perry v. Corning; Whitman).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent construed in view of nature of actual invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent construed in view of the nature of the actual invention
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims and specification are construed in light of what the inventor actually invented (Pidge v. Ferry).

rubrics_metrics.name: No infringement if invention imperfectly described
rubrics_metrics.description: No infringement if invention be imperfectly described
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent does not properly describe the invention, enforcement may be limited or fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requisites of verdict
rubrics_metrics.description: Requisites of verdict [in patent cases]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural requirements for verdicts in patent litigation (Pidge v. Ferry and others).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of Patent Office employees to patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Right of Patent Office employee to patent
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits on PO employees obtaining patents (Holknee Burglar Alarm Telegraph Co.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Judgment of Patent Office between interfering patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Judgment of Patent Office between interfering patents
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effect and finality of PTO decisions in interference/priority contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior publication as describing same invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior publication to describe same invention
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior publications that disclose the same invention can defeat patentability (Palmer, Ex parte).
